argv_note: stone-llama default llama-backend argv, from internal/serve/llama_backend.go Spawn() and confirmed on the live child /proc cmdline (pid 644766): llama-server --host 127.0.0.1 --port <internal> --api-key-file <runtime>/upstream_key -m <gguf>. same_quant_stone_vs_ollama.verdict: On identical Q4_K_M weights, stone-llama is at decode PARITY with ollama's warm path: 53.5 (stone, clean window) vs 55.2 (ollama, clean re-measure) tok/s = +3.2% ollama, within session noise. The 6.0 tok/s / 2922 MiB ollama figure was measured with stone's daemon resident on the card (confounded; see confounded_measurement) and is not a comparison. ollama wins warm TTFT (0.039 vs 0.116 s); stone holds 4x the context (32768 vs 8192) for +193 MiB VRAM. The round-1 'stone loses warm decode' verdict was the EXL3-vs-Q4_K_M quant confound, not the wrapper.

flash_attn_ab.base: stone-llama default argv (LLAMA_ARG_FLASH_ATTN unset -> llama-server default 'auto')
flash_attn_ab.verdict: Flash attention gives a measurable +9% decode and -8% wall on this 3B Q4_K_M pair; VRAM difference is noise (14 MiB). llama-server's default is 'auto', which already enables it, so there is NO flag change to make — stone-llama gets this for free. On identical weights stone-llama is at decode parity with ollama (53.5 vs 55.8 tok/s), so -fa does not change the verdict either way.

nommap_ab.verdict: No measurable difference on this model/size (decode identical, wall within 0.1%, VRAM identical). --no-mmap is not worth exercising further; mmap is fine.

round1_comparison.note: Round 1's ollama number (55.8 tok/s) was measured with stone fully unloaded and ollama warm; round 2's stone number (53.5 tok/s) is within ~4% of it. On identical weights stone-llama matches ollama's warm decode while offering 4x the context (32768 vs 8192) at +193 MiB VRAM. The round-1 'stone loses warm decode' verdict was an artifact of comparing EXL3 4.0bpw (3.5 bpw) against Q4_K_M, not of the wrapper.

prefill_cold_8kb.note: Each repeat sends a DIFFERENT 8KB prompt (run-index prefix) so server-side prompt cache cannot absorb the prefill. max_tokens=64. Raw files: raw-prefill-stone-cold.json / raw-prefill-ollama-cold.json.
prefill_cold_8kb.verdict: Cold 8KB prefill (unique prompt per repeat, max_tokens=64): stone TTFT 3.5 s vs ollama 1.2 s warm-loop mean (ollama's own run 1 cold-load TTFT was 7.1 s, worse than stone's, because it had been unloaded). After the first token, decode collapses on stone to ~5 tok/s (11-14 s for 62 chunks) vs ollama steady ~53 tok/s. That stone decode drop on long prompts is the real finding: same weights, stone's llama.cpp path serves long-context continuations ~10x slower than ollama's. Likely ctx/cache handling difference (stone leaves llama-server defaults; ollama pins -c 8192 -b 512 -ub 512). Follow-up next round: measure stone with explicit -c/-b/-ub env overrides to isolate.

prefill_warm_2kb_8kb.note: Same 2KB / 8KB prompt repeated 3x per size, so run 1 is the true prefill and runs 2-3 are server-side prompt-cache hits. max_tokens=64. Harness: prefill_measure.py.
prefill_warm_2kb_8kb.verdict: Run-1 (true prefill) TTFT on the same prompt: stone 0.52 s (2KB) / 0.82 s (8KB), ollama 0.32 s / 0.77 s — near parity. Cached repeats: stone 0.055/0.059 s vs ollama 0.019/0.029 s — ollama's prompt cache serves hits ~2-3x faster. The stone numbers are consistent with llama-server's default prompt cache; the difference is not a stone bug but ollama's keep-alive + smaller ctx making cache hits cheaper. See prefill_cold_8kb for the cold, unique-prompt comparison, where stone's post-first-token decode collapses to ~5 tok/s.

concurrency_4way.note: 4 parallel streaming requests x 128 tokens, 3 reps. Aggregate tok/s = total chunks / wall. p95 TTFT across per-request TTFTs.

stone_degraded_case.note: First attempt ran while the daemon had collapsed to 188 MiB resident (weights evicted, cause unresolved — see vram_collapse_finding); aggregate 9.4 tok/s, wall ~54 s. Excluded from the headline; kept as evidence.

concurrency_4way.vram_collapse_finding: After a previous session's stone daemon (pid 728130/738774 line) served the 8KB-prefill batch and a 4-way concurrency round, the llama-server child dropped from 2756 to 188 MiB resident with decode at 2.4-8.4 tok/s and prompt eval 38-40 ms/token. A restart of the same daemon (no config change) restored 2752 MiB and 55 tok/s. Reproduced once, cause not isolated (no Xid, no OOM in log; llama-server reports 'graphs reused' normally). Marking as a stability finding for the README, not a benchmark number.
concurrency_4way.verdict: 4-way concurrency on clean cards: stone-llama aggregates ~99.7 tok/s (near-linear 2x over its 53.5 single-stream, llama-server runs n_parallel=4 slots) with p95 TTFT 0.6-0.7 s; ollama aggregates ~55.7 tok/s (no aggregate gain over single-stream: it runs ONE slot, -np 1, requests queue) with p95 TTFT 4.6 s and per-request TTFTs spread 0.03-6.9 s (queueing). Stone does not serialise; ollama does. Stone wins concurrency on both throughput and TTFT stability.

control_measurement_disclosure: The -fa on/off and --no-mmap A/B were run by invoking stone-llama serve with engine_env set (LLAMA_ARG_FLASH_ATTN / LLAMA_ARG_MMAP), which is the supported passthrough — NOT by invoking llama-server directly. stone-llama's own default argv remained unchanged; only the child environment changed. All numbers above are stone-llama measurements.

clean_ollama_remeasure.conditions: stone daemon fully stopped first; ollama unloaded via keep_alive=0; nvidia-smi confirmed card clear (0 compute apps) before load; measured with ctrl_measure.py (same harness as stone, 5 repeats, 128 tokens, temp 0.7, same prompt).

vs_stone.verdict: Decode parity: 53.5 (stone) vs 55.2 (ollama) = +3.2% in ollama's favour, within session-to-session noise. Not 9x. ollama wins warm TTFT (0.039 vs 0.116 s). Stone holds 4x context (32768 vs 8192) for +193 MiB VRAM.
